cleaned_caption:
She found your phone. Now every level breaks 😂

Your ES/NQ wife post blew up, so here’s part 2. This one explains why some days ES respects every level and other days she rips through all of them.

It comes down to the dealers. They sold you those options, so they have to hedge, and their hedging sets the mood in the house.

🟢 Positive gamma = calm marriage

They sell the rips and buy the dips. Every fight ends in makeup. Levels hold and price comes home to value.

→ I fade the edges.

🔴 Negative gamma = she found the texts

They sell into drops and buy into rallies. Every argument escalates. Levels break and stops get run.

→ I stop fading, follow the move, and trade fewer contracts.

The line between the two is the gamma flip. It moves during the session, so check it every morning instead of guessing.

Same market, two different relationships. Most traders use one playbook for both, and that’s where the account dies.

title: Traders paid $1.8 billion yesterday to insure ONE house.

Traders paid $1.8 billion yesterday to insure ONE house.

Not SPY. QQQ.

Here’s the way I read options flow before I touch ES or NQ:

The market is a village under a volcano. A sell-off is the eruption. Every index is a house.

House next to the lava → people buy insurance (puts). That’s hedging.

House far away → people buy lottery tickets (calls). That’s upside bets.

Yesterday’s ledger on quantedFlow:

SPY → 50% calls, $748M. Half insured, half lottery. Balanced.

QQQ → 78% puts, $1.78B. Almost everyone insured the Nasdaq house.

What that means today:

ES → nobody’s panicking. Two-way trade. Work your levels, fade the extremes.

NQ → heavily insured, so the dealer who sold those puts is short gamma. Below the put wall, don’t fade it. Every tick down forces him to sell more. Above the wall, the puts decay and you get the squeeze.

Flow tells you the mood. GEX tells you the address.

title: ES is the wife. NQ is the toxic ex 😂
cleaned_caption:
ES is the wife. NQ is the toxic ex 😂

Someone asked me why I trade ES instead of NQ. Short answer: she respects the levels.

SPX has the deepest options market in the world. Dealers hedge that size in ES, so the gamma levels actually have money behind them. NQ’s options book is way thinner, so she blows through levels, wicks your stop and acts like nothing happened.

I still watch NQ though. When they move together, the move is real. When NQ makes a new high and ES doesn’t follow, someone’s lying. Usually NQ.

So I read the auction on ES. If I take NQ, I use fewer contracts for the same dollar risk.

title: How do you define your bias for the day?” 👀
cleaned_caption:
“How do you define your bias for the day?” 👀

It’s one of the questions I get most in my DMs. So I recorded my whole morning check on today’s ES chart.

The rule: a candle only steps up if it closes ABOVE the previous high.

A green candle that closes under it isn’t bullish. It’s a pause.

Monthly = the current 🌊

Weekly = the tide

Daily = the wave

15 min = the auction

5 min = the trigger

Today? Mixed. Small size, walls only, max loss set before the bell.

I do this every morning.
spoken_transcript: You don't pick your outfit in the middle of the storm. You check the weather first. That's your bias. And this is exactly how I built mine this morning on ES. Monthly, weekly, daily, then 15 minutes and five. Step one, the staircase. Price only goes up when each candle steps fully onto the next stair. Higher high, higher low, and a close above the previous high. Monthly chart, the ocean current. April and May, clean steps up. August, another step. But September, higher high, then it closed under August high. Half a foot on the step. That's a pause, not a trend. So the current is still up. It's just resting.
